paper_metadata.title: Structure and properties of Fe–Al–Ti intermetallic alloys

evidence.quote: Structure and mechanical properties of Fe–Al–Ti alloys in the composition range Fe–(10–27.5) at.%Al–(10–30) at.%Ti have been studied.

Eutectic morphologies were observed in alloys 1–4, suggesting that after the formation of the primary phase interdendritic liquid solidified as eutectic. In the case of alloys 1 and 2, the eutectic observed was a-Fe+Fe2Ti.
In the case of the three-phase alloys (alloys 3 and 4), the eutectic phases were Fe2Ti+Fe2AlTi in alloy 3 and a-Fe+Fe2Ti in alloy 4, respectively.
In the case of the three-phase alloys (alloys 3 and 4), the eutectic phases were Fe2Ti+Fe2AlTi in alloy 3 and a-Fe+Fe2Ti in alloy 4, respectively.
Alloy 6 did not exhibit any plasticity at room temperature and failure occurred because of cracking at low stresses in the alloy samples.
Values of the stress exponent n observed were between 3 and 6 and were not significantly dependent on the composition. Such stress exponents are characteristic of dislocation creep.
The Young’s modulus is just above 200 GPa for the alloys studied.

The value of Q derived from the creep stress rate data at constant stress for the present set of alloys was found to be in the range of 400 to 600 KJ/mol.
